And there’s also Micron breaking ground on a $9bn Hiroshima fab expansion and SEMI asking the US government not to intervene in the memory chip market… As always, let’s take them in reverse order, as according to Google Analytics: 5. Samsung expects 18x increase in Q2 profits Samsung Electronics said it expects Q2 revenues to be up 129% YoY at $124 billion for a profit up 18x YoY at $58 billion. The results come on the back of a 40% QoQ rise in DRAM prices and a 50% rise in NAND prices. Samsung announced last week that it plans to spend over $70 billion in 2026 on production capacity expansion and research. Shortly after the announcement the company’s shares were hit by a 9% sell-off but this was mostly recovered in a price surge on Friday. 4. Nexperia’s 1200 V SiC MOSFETs in QDPAK packaging Nexperia is releasing 1200 V silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs in QDPAK packaging, as part of its wide-bandgap (WBG) portfolio. They feature a top-side cooled surface-mount package optimised for high-power density and thermally demanding applications, says the company. For example, EV onboard chargers (OBC), high-voltage DC-DC converters, EV charging infrastructure, photovoltaic inverters and uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). 3. David Potter, Psion founder, dies aged 82 David Potter, founder of Psion, has died at the age of 82. Born in South Africa, Potter won a scholarship to Trinity College, Cambridge and was awarded his doctorate by Imperial College, London. He lectured in the USA and UK, while successfully investing on the stock market, then set up Psion to participate in the microelectronics revolution. Twenty years later, Psion entered the FTSE 100. David PotterPotter got the tech bug with the advent of the microprocessor in the 1970s. 2. Micron breaks ground on $9bn Hiroshima fab expansion At the weekend, Micron broke ground on a $9.3 billion expansion of its fab in Hiroshima supported by a $4.8 billion allocation by the Japanese government. “Micron’s very first HBM production wafer was made right here in Hiroshima,” said Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra at the ceremony, “when American boldness meets Japanese craftsmanship, you do not get a compromise. You get the best in the world.” Japan’s Economy, Industry and Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa, said Japan is ready to do “all that it can” to help chip companies build fabs in the country. 1. SEMI asks US government not to intervene in memory crisis SEMI has written a letter to the US government asking it not to intervene in the memory chip market. The letter is being seen as opposition to Apple’s request to the US government to be allowed to buy memory from Chinese vendors CXMT and YMTC. “While targeted policies can support accelerating domestic supply resilience, interventions that distort pricing or capacity decisions risk prolonging the demand downturn.” Recommended Articles Most Read – Nvidia PCs, Palantir NHS, Samsung Foundry What caught your eye?
